in_list_filter.label: IN and BETWEEN
in_list_filter.summary: Use IN for exact value sets and BETWEEN for inclusive ranges.

sc_in_meaning.title: What IN does
sc_in_meaning.hint: Think about whether the row can match one value or must match both values.

help.concept: `IN` checks whether one column value matches any one item in a list of exact values.
help.hint_1: Compare the condition with the column named in the question, then check which rows would remain.
help.hint_2: A row needs to match one listed city, not every city at the same time.

options.a: The city must be both Chicago and Miami at the same time
options.b: The city can be Chicago or Miami
options.c: The city must come alphabetically between Chicago and Miami
options.d: The city must not be Chicago or Miami

sc_not_in_result.title: Identify a row kept by NOT IN
sc_not_in_result.prompt: Which customer would be returned by `WHERE status NOT IN ('draft', 'inactive')`?
sc_not_in_result.hint: Look for a customer whose status is neither `draft` nor `inactive`.

help.concept: `NOT IN` removes rows whose value appears in the listed set and keeps rows with other values.
help.hint_1: In this dataset, the remaining status after excluding `draft` and `inactive` is `active`.
help.hint_2: Choose the customer whose row has `status = 'active'`.

sc_between_inclusive.title: BETWEEN includes the ends
sc_between_inclusive.prompt: What does `WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2026-01-12' AND '2026-01-22'` mean?
sc_between_inclusive.hint: Check whether the start and end dates are included in a BETWEEN range.

help.concept: In SQL, BETWEEN checks whether a value is inside a range and includes both boundary values.
help.hint_1: Think about whether rows on exactly `2026-01-12` and exactly `2026-01-22` should stay in the results.
help.hint_2: BETWEEN acts like a start-and-end range check using both a lower bound and an upper bound.

options.b: Dates from `2026-01-12` through `2026-01-22`, including both ends

sc_between_equivalent.title: Equivalent range condition
sc_between_equivalent.prompt: Which WHERE clause is equivalent to `signup_date BETWEEN '2026-01-15' AND '2026-01-25'`?
sc_between_equivalent.hint: Look for one condition that keeps dates on or after the start and on or before the end.

help.concept: BETWEEN can be rewritten as two comparisons joined with AND: one lower bound and one upper bound.
help.hint_1: The first comparison should keep dates from the start date upward.
help.hint_2: The second comparison should still allow the ending date itself, not exclude it.

try-in_list_filter-sketch0.hint: Put both quoted status values inside the IN parentheses.

help.concept: IN keeps a row when the column matches any one exact value in the list.
help.hint_1: Put both quoted status values inside the IN parentheses.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned columns and rows with the expected result.

practice-inclusive-range.title: Practice: Filter an inclusive range
practice-inclusive-range.prompt: Return `id`, `full_name`, and `signup_date` from `customers`, in that order. Keep signups from `2026-01-12` through `2026-01-25`, including both boundary dates.
practice-inclusive-range.hint: Use an inclusive lower and upper boundary. You can express the range in either standard equivalent form.

help.concept: An inclusive SQL range can be written with BETWEEN or with two inclusive comparisons joined by AND.
help.hint_1: Both the starting date and ending date must remain in the result.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned columns and rows with the expected result.

in_value_list.title: Match exact sets with IN
in_value_list.bodyMarkdown:
`IN` checks whether a value matches any exact value in a list.

Use `IN (...)` for allowed values and `NOT IN (...)` for excluded values. It is usually clearer than repeating the same column with several OR comparisons.

not_in_value_list.title: Match inclusive ranges with BETWEEN
not_in_value_list.bodyMarkdown:
`BETWEEN` checks an inclusive range: both endpoints count.

Use it when a requirement gives one lower and one upper boundary, such as a date window or numeric range.

`BETWEEN low AND high` is equivalent to `>= low AND <= high`. Keep the boundaries in lower-to-upper order.
